The mass was carefully dissected from surrounding tissues, and the adrenal gland was removed and sent to the pathology department. There were no intraoperative complications.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 45-year-old female with a history of medication-controlled hypertension and Type 2 diabetes presented with an incidentally discovered right adrenal mass during a periodic echocardiogram. Contrast-enhanced CT imaging revealed a large, well-defined, heterogeneous mass measuring 13 × 12 × 9.5 cm in the right adrenal gland with areas suggesting recent hemorrhage and fat-density consistent with adipose tissue, without invasion or lymphadenopathy. Laboratory investigations were within normal limits. The patient underwent right open adrenalectomy without intraoperative complications. Histopathological examination of the surgical specimen confirmed the diagnosis of hemorrhagic myelolipoma, demonstrating a mixture of mature adipose tissue and hematopoietic elements (myeloid and erythroid cells) with focal areas of hemorrhage and hemosiderin deposits, consistent with the radiological findings. Postoperative recovery was uneventful with discharge on postoperative day 5. Follow-up imaging at 6 months showed no evidence of tumor recurrence, and the patient remains asymptomatic under regular surveillance.
